solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Criticise an old lady's hat

parts.note: to pan a show is to criticise it harshly
one's old lady is one's mother, MA

explanation.surface: Someone mocks an elderly woman's choice of headwear.
explanation.definitionFit: A Panama is a brimmed straw hat, so it is one example of the wider category of hat.

clue.text: One pledged, I understand to appear at end of concert

indicators.note: one piece comes after the concert piece, at its end

parts.note: a prom is a promenade concert, as at the BBC Proms
I see means I understand

explanation.surface: Someone promised a slot at the end of a concert.
explanation.definitionFit: A promisee is the person to whom a promise is made, the legal term for the one pledged to.

clue.text: Top dog ultimately rejected piece of meat

parts.note: number one, abbreviated NO I, is the top

indicators.note: the final letter is thrown out

parts.note: a setter is a breed of gun dog

explanation.surface: The leading dog turned its nose up at a cut of meat.
explanation.walkthrough: Top is number one, written NO I with I for one; 'ultimately rejected' takes the final R off SETTER.
explanation.definitionFit: A noisette is a small round boneless slice of lamb, a cut of meat.

clue.text: Materials processed in plant

indicators.note: materials put through a process are changed in form, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Raw materials being processed inside a factory.
explanation.walkthrough: 'plant' looks like the factory; it is the definition, a living plant.
explanation.definitionFit: Mare's tail is an aquatic plant with whorls of narrow leaves on upright stems.

clue.text: A great may wearing attractive, small garments

indicators.note: the attractive word wears the other piece, which sits inside it like a body in clothing

parts.note: cute means attractive
a lot is a great many (the clue as published drops the n of many)
S is the usual abbreviation for small, as on clothing labels

explanation.surface: A crowd of people in fetching clothes, with the small sizes noted.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue as published reads 'may', evidently for 'many': 'a great many' is LOT.
explanation.definitionFit: Culottes are women's knee-length trousers cut to look like a skirt, so they are a kind of garment.

clue.text: Film company started in US it turned out

indicators.note: turned inside out, so the letters come out in a new order

explanation.surface: A Hollywood studio's origins in America, as it happened.
explanation.definitionFit: United Artists is a Hollywood studio founded in 1919 by Chaplin, Pickford, Fairbanks and Griffith.

clue.text: The last character loathsome gangsters could restrain

indicators.note: the words hold the letters captive within them

explanation.surface: A villain whom nasty gangsters might hold back.
explanation.definitionFit: Omega is the final letter of the Greek alphabet, so it is the last character.

clue.text: Idea that's incomplete nevertheless

indicators.note: the word is not finished, so its final letter is missing

parts.note: a thought is an idea

explanation.surface: A half-formed idea is still worth something.
explanation.definitionFit: Used as an adverb at the end of a sentence it means however, a synonym of nevertheless.

clue.text: In bar, one stands up for a Spanish lady

indicators.note: in a down answer, up means the letters read from bottom to top
the letters lie inside the words that follow

explanation.surface: In a pub, a man rises to give his seat to a Spanish woman.
explanation.walkthrough: ARONES sits in 'bar, one stands'; 'up' reads it backwards in this down clue, while 'stands' does double service in the surface only as hidden-word text.
explanation.definitionFit: Señora is the Spanish title for a married woman, the equivalent of Mrs or madam.

clue.text: Tree, one screened by rambling rose

indicators.note: one piece is hidden from view behind, and so inside, the other
a rambling rose wanders, so its letters wander into a new order

parts.note: the Roman numeral for one is I

explanation.surface: A tree half hidden by a climbing rose in a garden.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rambling' makes OSER from ROSE, and I goes inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: An osier is a willow whose pliant twigs are used in basketry, so it is a kind of tree.

clue.text: Listened to True Blue record

indicators.note: what is heard rather than read, so the word is taken for how it is spoken

parts.note: right means true or correct
feeling blue is feeling down

explanation.surface: Someone heard a True Blue record, perhaps the Madonna album.
explanation.walkthrough: 'record' looks like the album being played; it is the verb, to put on paper.
explanation.definitionFit: To record something on paper is to note it, the phrasal verb meaning to put into writing.

clue.text: Potential buyer of computer software, one expecting to save a bit of money

parts.note: Windows is Microsoft's operating system

indicators.note: to save is to keep safe inside, so the expecting piece holds the money piece

parts.note: a hoper is one who hopes or expects
P is a penny, a small coin of British money

explanation.surface: A PC software shopper hoping to keep their spending low.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone browsing shop displays without buying is a would-be customer, so a potential buyer.

clue.text: Basically I head away from here after losing capital

parts.note: a ness is a headland, like Loch Ness's neighbour promontories in Scotland

indicators.note: the capital, or first, letter of the word is dropped

parts.note: hence is an old word for away from here

explanation.surface: Someone says they are leaving town now that they have lost their money.
explanation.walkthrough: 'losing capital' takes H from HENCE, leaving ENCE. NESS is a headland, as in place names.
explanation.definitionFit: Both phrases mean fundamentally, at the core of the matter, so the idiom is a synonym.

clue.text: Experimental film maker's passion

definitions.meaning: Kenneth ... was an American avant-garde film-maker

explanation.surface: An avant-garde director's great love in life.
explanation.definitionFit: Kenneth Anger made underground films such as Scorpio Rising, and passion can mean fury or rage.

clue.text: Infer second portion of food includes a form of egg?

indicators.note: the larger phrase takes the egg piece within it

parts.note: a second helping is an extra plate
O is egg-shaped, the letter standing for an egg

explanation.surface: A diner asks for seconds, including some egg dish.
explanation.walkthrough: O goes into EXTRA PLATE between P and L.
explanation.definitionFit: To extrapolate is to deduce something beyond the known data, a synonym of drawing an inference.

clue.text: River swimmer finds edges of lake very unpleasant

parts.note: the Exe is a river in Devon, in south-west England
a crab is a sea creature, a swimmer

indicators.note: only the outermost letters of the word are kept

explanation.surface: A river swimmer finds the lake's margins horrible.
explanation.definitionFit: Execrable means extremely bad or detestable, a synonym of very unpleasant.

clue.text: Climber with an inclination to protect leg

indicators.note: the inclination piece shields the leg piece by enclosing it

parts.note: a list is a lean or tilt, as of a ship
a pin is slang for a leg

explanation.surface: A mountaineer on a slope protecting an injured leg.
explanation.walkthrough: PIN for leg is old slang, as in 'shaky on his pins'.
explanation.definitionFit: An alpinist is a mountaineer, especially in the Alps, so a kind of climber.

clue.text: Beast half wiped-out in past I assume

indicators.note: the first half of the word is erased, leaving the rest

parts.note: ego is Latin for I
to don clothes is to assume them

explanation.surface: Someone supposes a creature was half exterminated long ago.
explanation.walkthrough: 'half wiped-out' removes PA from PAST, leaving ST.
explanation.definitionFit: The stegodon was a prehistoric elephant-like mammal, so an extinct beast.

clue.text: Find allotment's been taken over by someone else, and become confused

definitions.text: Find allotment's been taken over by someone else
definitions.meaning: losing one's garden plot to another person, read literally

explanation.surface: A gardener loses their allotment to a rival and goes to pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means to lose one's grip on reality, and the literal reading is losing a plot of land.

clue.text: Outlaw and fighter brought round and put in cell

parts.note: to outlaw something is to ban it

indicators.note: turned round, so the word is read backwards

parts.note: a pug is a boxer, short for pugilist

explanation.surface: A bandit and a boxer are revived and jailed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'brought round' looks like reviving someone; here it turns the fighter backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Bang up is British slang for locking someone in a prison cell.

clue.text: Grotesque head on stick

indicators.note: grotesque means distorted, so the letters are distorted

parts.note: re means on or about, as in a memo

explanation.surface: A gruesome head impaled on a pole.
explanation.definitionFit: To adhere is to cling or remain attached, a synonym of the verb stick.

clue.text: Poet making mark briefly, attending top-class university

parts.note: A is first class, top grade

indicators.note: cut short, so the word loses its final letter

parts.note: a dent is a mark left by a blow

explanation.surface: A poet making a name for himself while at an elite university.
explanation.definitionFit: W. H. Auden was an Anglo-American poet of the twentieth century, an example of a poet.

clue.text: Unknown number attending church, that goes without saying

parts.note: N stands for an unknown number in algebra
to be at something is to attend it

explanation.surface: Of course an uncertain number of people go to church.
explanation.definitionFit: Natch is informal shorthand for naturally, an exclamation meaning of course.

clue.text: Monitoring old boy working behind bar?

parts.note: OB is the abbreviation for old boy, a former pupil
a barman at work is serving customers

explanation.surface: A former pupil watches the room while pulling pints.
explanation.definitionFit: Observing means watching closely, a synonym of keeping under watch.

clue.text: Primates nibble fruit on the outside

indicators.note: the fruit sits around the eating piece, enclosing it

parts.note: grapes are a fruit
to nibble is to eat

explanation.surface: Monkeys nibble the skin of fruit.
explanation.definitionFit: Gorillas, chimpanzees and orang-utans are the great apes, a family of primates.

clue.text: TV pioneer making broadcast in Bangladesh

indicators.note: one piece goes inside the country code

parts.note: BD is the international vehicle code for Bangladesh
to air a programme is to broadcast it

explanation.surface: An early television pioneer transmits a programme in Bangladesh.
explanation.definitionFit: John Logie Baird demonstrated the first working television system in 1926, making him a TV pioneer.

clue.text: Display of information set out in Chapter 1

indicators.note: arranged differently, so the letters are laid out anew

parts.note: 1 is the Roman numeral I

explanation.surface: Data laid out in the first chapter of a book.
explanation.definitionFit: A pie chart is a circular graph divided into slices, a way of presenting data visually.

clue.text: Physicist reportedly was aware of weight

indicators.note: the word is taken as spoken, so its silent first letter goes

parts.note: knew means was aware
a ton is a unit of weight

explanation.surface: A physicist apparently knew about weight, fittingly for gravity.
explanation.definitionFit: Isaac Newton formulated the laws of motion and gravitation, a celebrated physicist.
